incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: High error rates + perf cliff on continuous-batching runtime (kv-cache growth). Severity: P2 -> possible customer impact. See runbook: https://runbooks.internal/cont-batch-kv

Maya (oncall): reading the metrics now, tail latency for text-gen spiked from 120ms -> 1.2s, error rate ~4%. Observed mem pressure on batcher hosts.

Oliver: tagging in. Which model fleet?

Maya (oncall): looks like 'redwood-open-a1' serving group in us-west-2 dedicated pool. KV-cache entries ramped up after a deploy ~ 03:12 UTC. I see batch controller's `max_batch_tokens` showing 2e6 in the live config (wtf).

Dave: that explains it. If max_batch_tokens is insane it can let the batcher accumulate huge prefix KV state per request and never flush properly, leading to cache blowup and evictions thrashing.

Anita: any customers hit? Priya can you confirm?

Priya (CS): 3 customers reported 5xxs (mostly timeouts) and one partner saw degraded latency in their production flow. I opened a support case and flagged as urgent.

Maya (oncall): quick snapshot logs: 
```
batcher_controller.INFO: config_update: {"max_batch_tokens": 2000000, "max_num_seqs": 512, "batch_timeout_ms": 500}
kv_cache.DEBUG: insert_count=1245236 size_bytes=3.9GB active_keys=248k evictions=12k
runtime.warn: kv-cache-mem-pressure: host gpu-17 at 93% mem
```

Oliver: we need a hotfix. Option A: roll back config to last-known-good (`max_batch_tokens`: 4096, `max_num_seqs`: 64, `batch_timeout_ms`: 50). Option B: temporarily disable continuous batching for that model-group and bounce batchers.

Maya (oncall): I'm going to push a quick config patch to reduce `max_batch_tokens` and `max_num_seqs` (hotfix) and set `batch_timeout_ms` lower. Will do canary first on two hosts.

deploy-bot: deploying config patch to fleet/redwood-open-a1 canary (hosts: batcher-03, batcher-07).

Maya (oncall): patch applied to canary. Monitoring...

(2m later)

Maya (oncall): canary looks good: kv cache growth flattened, latency back to ~150ms on canary hosts, errors down. Proceeding to rollout.

Oliver: roll the rest, but add an automatic throttle: if `kv_cache.active_keys` > 200k then temporarily reject continuous-batching and route to single-request path. Add a short circuity to stop reentrancy.

Maya (oncall): rolling to remaining hosts now. Also triggering a targeted restart of batcher workers on hosts that show high eviction thrash to reclaim mem.

Dave: capture metrics for a postmortem: exact config diff, deploy timestamp, affected host list, top offending request prefixes. Also check whether model quantization changed kernel behavior causing larger KV size per token.

Priya (CS): customer updates: notified impacted customers, ETA for full mitigation ~20m, offering mitigation guidance and apology.

(10m later)

Maya (oncall): rollout complete. Cluster-wide medians: tail latency back to 140ms, error rate <0.2%. KV cache size reduced to ~900MB on avg.

Priya (CS): customers acknowledged, one asked for incident report.

Oliver: good. Root cause hypothesis: bad config push (accidental override) that set `max_batch_tokens` to an incorrect order-of-magnitude value during a config merge + missing validator for sane upper bounds.

Anita: immediate action items: 1) postmortem draft, 2) add server-side config validation (hard upper bounds for batching params), 3) add runaway mitigation: throttle continuous-batching when `kv_cache.active_keys` crosses threshold, 4) update runbook with explicit rollback steps for batcher config.

Maya (oncall): handoff to Oliver for next 4 hours — I'm going offline in 10m. Oliver, you've got the pager. Please keep incident thread updated. :white_check_mark:

Oliver: taking over. I'll own the follow-ups and the postmortem. Next steps: gather logs (batcher/controller/runtime), diff config from deploy system, produce timeline and affected customers list.

Dave: long-term: consider enforcing per-request KV size limits and better instrumentation for sequence-length distributions. Also we should check the canary policy — a more conservative canary might have caught the regression earlier.

Maya (oncall): small note: we used the emergency knob `disable_continuous_batching=true` as an alternate path for one partner while we rolled. It should be documented.

deploy-bot: config rollback available as release 2026.03.15-rbk-001.

Oliver: status -> mitigated (P2 -> monitoring). I'll post a follow-up summary and file the postmortem ticket. Assigning owners: config-validators -> Anita, telemetry+alerts -> Dave, customer comms -> Priya.

Priya (CS): tagging case IDs in the postmortem so we can correlate customer reports.

Oliver: thanks everyone. Closing the active page, keeping thread open for postmortem notes. :hammer_and_wrench:
